I found an abandoned Minecraft server one time. It was survival mode, and I spawned in this awfully barren and dark place. I figured it must've been popular since the spawn point was picked clean. I desperately needed wood to start making any tools so I had to venture away. The server is completely dead. After swimming for minutes across a lake, I arrived somewhere with trees. I finally started collecting items, and I saw a nice hill in the distance covered in colorful flowers. Obviously I journeyed over there. What I found was pretty weird. There was another player model, with a username I can't remember, standing amidst the flowers. I was the only one connected to the server, as far as I could tell. I figured I'd craft a sign and write a message to this man in case he ever returned.  

The second time I joined this server, it was still empty. I found my way back to the same spot, and nothing had changed. So I made a new sign, saying farewell to the man as if he were lost. I remember feeling very odd and melancholy in this moment, like I was leaving someone important to me behind: though we shared nothing but a player model and I never even knew if it was a person to begin with. 

It doesn't end there. I kept playing on this server, treating it like a survival world, hoping someone would show up and I could show them my findings. One night I was mining, just going diagonally into the ground, when I found a cave structure. I found a lot of gold so that was cool. Then, somewhere around the corner, I eventually saw a light: it was lava. But I turned the corner; and I was met with a small room. The light was from a pool of lava, I wasn't joking about that, but there was something else.  There was a player model, this one named "Cam", standing idly, surrounded by flowers that were somehow planted in stone. 

I wrote a few signs saying farewell to Cam and the other man, and describing how I had enjoyed the time I had spent with them. Then I left, and never joined the server again. 


I know they were probably just weird remnants of logged off users, but somehow they really affected my feelings. And the flowers were peculiar. It was a little disturbing after I left the server for good. I felt alone, or like I had become one of them: frozen in time and surrounded by flowers.

items.title: What's Xbox's obsession with signing in to play games?
items.text:
What's Xbox's obsession with signing in to play games?
I went to a friends house today to play games. He has an Xbox. I've never owned one.

So we were playing Mortal Kombat 11, local versus, and as expected there was a [press A to join] prompt for player 2. But Instead of just letting me pick a fighter, it insisted I sign in to a Microsoft account, which I don't have. I couldn't even use my friend's because it was "in use". There was not even a clear "guest" option. Eventually we figured out how to continue without signing in.


Then later we were playing Portal 2 (one of my top 5 favorite games, by the way) in local co-op. I can't recall if I had to sign-in this time as a second player. But I do know that after we got about 6 levels in to the co-op campaign, the internet had a hiccup I guess and the entire game crashed because we were "no longer signed in".

What the hell? Why does Xbox want to make it so hard to play games??



Edit: Not to mention that I, as second player, could not use fighter customizations in Mortal Kombat because I wasn't tied to a Microsoft account.
